evidence: app/src/pages/abilities/[name].astro — whole feature lives in one route file; no other page links to /abilities
app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:126 — the only inbound link (Abilities section) is one self-contained block to delete
app/src/layouts/Base.astro:24-27 — nav is a static list, so a section link is a one-line edit
app/src/components/CardList.astro:30-33 — by contrast, the Team feature leaks into the generic card component (data-team-remove button), so removing Team touches 6 files
removability.rationale: Abilities removal is the anchor's 5 (delete a directory plus one section block in the Pokémon page, nothing else references it). The team feature is less self-contained, so the codebase isn't uniformly clean.

evidence: app/src/lib/pokedex.ts:104-116 — every reference-based card list (type/move/ability) is built in one function, cardsForPokemon, where a species/default-pokemon id fix would land
app/src/components/CardList.astro:18 — all five card lists render sprites through one line (spriteUrl), so a sprite fix covers every list
app/src/lib/api.ts:5-7 — base URL, cache freshness and SWR logic are all confined to api.ts
app/src/components/TeamButton.astro:21,29-34 and app/src/pages/team.astro:72-86 — the team cookie contract is re-implemented twice in client scripts, so a format or size change means 3-4 edits
changeability.rationale: The two headline fixes (sprite, data source) land in one obvious place thanks to centralized card construction and rendering. Deducted for the team cookie and partial-refresh scripts that must be changed in triplicate.

evidence: app/src/lib/pokedex.ts:99-116 — lib functions take narrow, documented inputs (refs + note callback) and pages consume them, a clean seam
app/src/components/CardList.astro:7,30-33 — a generic display component carries the team feature's removable prop and data-team-remove DOM, so the feature isn't isolated from shared UI

app/src/components/TeamButton.astro:29-34 vs app/src/lib/team.ts:5-19 — the same cookie serialization exists in two client scripts and one server module with no shared source of truth (TEAM_SIZE/cookie name duplicated at TeamButton.astro:21, team.astro:72,44)

app/src/pages/index.astro:101-109, app/src/components/MovesSection.astro:190-202, app/src/pages/team.astro:92-99 — implicit ID contracts (results/moves-content/team-content) tie markup to inline scripts via duplicated fetch-DOMParser-replaceWith logic
coupling.rationale: Server-side structure is loosely coupled with narrow props, but the team cookie contract is implemented three times across server and client, a feature leaks into a shared component, and the partial-refresh pattern is copy-pasted with implicit DOM-ID contracts.

evidence: app/src/lib/pokedex.ts:99-116 — cardsForPokemon handles the real variation across type/move/ability lists (alternate forms, dedupe, ordering) with a note callback instead of flags
app/src/lib/pokedex.ts:66-70 — getTypeLabels returns a memoized labeler, a reusable seam for English type names
app/src/components/CardList.astro — one card component stretches to home, move, ability, type and team pages

app/src/pages/moves/[name].astro:18-39 vs app/src/pages/abilities/[name].astro:9-21 — detail-page scaffolding (Base/h1/NotFound/effect fallback) is repeated rather than shared; an Items page would copy it
app/src/components/MovesSection.astro:12,22,46-49 — takes pokemon: any and does its own API fetching, so it can't stretch to another resource or be tested without a live record
abstraction_design.rationale: The core abstractions (Card, cardsForPokemon, Section, TypeBadge, Base) are designed around the app's real variation and stretch well. Held at 4 because detail-page scaffolding and the partial-refresh script are copy-pasted, and boolean-flag creep (removable, link) is starting to show.

findings.issue: Team cookie read/write logic is duplicated between TeamButton.astro and team.astro:78-86, mirroring lib/team.ts:5-19; cookie name and TEAM_SIZE=6 are hardcoded in both scripts (TeamButton.astro:21, team.astro:72) and 'of 6' in markup (team.astro:44).
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared client module (Astro bundles <script> imports) exporting readTeam/writeTeam, TEAM_COOKIE and TEAM_SIZE from lib/team.ts, and render the count from the constant.

findings.issue: The generic card component contains the team feature's remove button behind a removable flag, so removing or changing the team feature requires editing shared UI.
findings.suggestion: Use a named <slot> rendered per item (or a slot/fallback prop) so per-item actions stay in the pages that own the feature.

findings.issue: The fetch → DOMParser → replaceWith partial-refresh pattern is copy-pasted three times (index.astro:101-109, MovesSection.astro:190-202, team.astro:92-99), each with its own implicit element-ID contract between markup and script.
findings.suggestion: Extract a small shared client helper (e.g. swapFragment(url, id)) and a convention (data-partial attribute) so a change to the refresh behavior lands once.

findings.issue: The component accepts pokemon: any and performs its own API fetching (version groups at :22, move records at :46-49), giving it an untyped, untestable seam.
findings.suggestion: Accept a typed minimal shape (moves list) or pre-compute the tables in lib and pass structured data as props.

findings.issue: Detail-page scaffolding (Base/h1, NotFound branch, 404 status, effect fallback chain) is duplicated across moves, abilities and types pages, so a new resource type copies ~25 lines.
findings.suggestion: Factor the common bits into small helpers (e.g. a resourceOr404 frontmatter helper and an Effect section component).

findings.issue: getSpeciesById refetches and rebuilds the full 1,025-entry species map on every card-list request (typed via the shared cache, but the mapping work repeats per call).
findings.suggestion: Cache the Map promise alongside the underlying list so callers share one construction.

summary: This is an easy codebase to change: all data shaping lives in one lib layer, every Pokémon card list renders through a single component, and transport/caching is confined to api.ts, so the sprite bug and a data-source change are each one-place fixes. Deductions come from the client side: the team cookie contract and the partial-refresh script are duplicated across three files, and the team feature leaks into CardList via the removable flag. Detail pages share structure by convention rather than abstraction, which an Items section would expose as mild copy-paste.
